clue.text: Standardised part of the French in 26

indicators.note: in tells us one piece sits inside the other, here the French word inside the synonym for 26

parts.note: 26 down is PIER, and a mole is a stone pier or breakwater
du is French for 'of the'

explanation.surface: A description of a standard component in some French context, referring to another clue.
explanation.walkthrough: '26' points to the answer of 26 down, which must first be swapped for a synonym before the French goes inside it; a cross-reference like this is a two-step substitution.
explanation.definitionFit: A module is a standard unit that fits with others to build something larger.

clue.text: Officer put on the case — it's valued above diamonds

parts.note: a major is an army officer
a suit is a case in law

explanation.surface: An officer is put in charge of the case, which outranks the gems.
explanation.walkthrough: In bridge, hearts and spades outrank diamonds and clubs; 'put on' places MAJOR above SUIT in this down entry.
explanation.definitionFit: In bridge, hearts and spades score higher than diamonds and clubs.

clue.text: Make plain slate with platinum

parts.note: to slate is to criticise harshly, to decry
Pt is the chemical symbol for platinum

explanation.surface: Making something plain using slate and platinum.
explanation.walkthrough: 'slate' looks like the roofing stone, but it is the verb for harsh criticism.
explanation.definitionFit: To decrypt a code is to turn it into readable text.

clue.text: You make no profit on this resale, sold by mistake

definitions.text: You make no profit on this

indicators.note: by mistake signals the letters are put in the wrong order

explanation.surface: A shopkeeper loses money on resale after selling something in error.
explanation.walkthrough: 'by mistake' rearranges RESALE SOLD.
explanation.definitionFit: Shops sell some goods below cost to draw customers in, hoping they buy other items.

clue.text: Romantic from abroad who doesn't start from abroad

parts.note: qui is the French for 'who', so 'who' given in a foreign tongue

indicators.note: doesn't start means the first letter of the following word is dropped

parts.note: exotic means coming from abroad

explanation.surface: A romantic foreigner who never gets going, travelling abroad.
explanation.walkthrough: 'from abroad' appears twice with two jobs: first it turns 'who' into French QUI, then it means EXOTIC, which 'doesn't start' cuts to XOTIC.
explanation.definitionFit: Quixotic means idealistic and impractical, like the dreamy knight Don Quixote.

clue.text: 27 put out? None put out

indicators.note: out signals the letters of the word put are knocked into a new order

parts.note: none is nothing, the letter O
to snuff a candle is to put it out

explanation.surface: Asking whether a clever person is upset, and being told nobody is upset.
explanation.walkthrough: '27' refers to 27 across, KNOWING. 'out' jumbles PUT into UPT, which with O for none and SNUFF completes the phrase.
explanation.definitionFit: Up to snuff describes someone shrewd, not easily fooled.

clue.text: Photograph of unknown fish

parts.note: x is the standard unknown quantity in algebra
a ray is a flat fish

explanation.surface: A picture of a mysterious fish.
explanation.definitionFit: A radiograph is a picture of the body's interior taken with penetrating radiation.

clue.text: Thickening agent mixed in a copita

indicators.note: mixed signals the letters of copita are stirred into a new order

explanation.surface: Something to thicken a drink is stirred into a sherry glass.
explanation.walkthrough: A copita is a tulip-shaped sherry glass; 'mixed' rearranges its letters into TAPIOC.
explanation.definitionFit: Tapioca is a starch from cassava roots used to thicken puddings and sauces.

clue.text: Impudence out of the side of the' mouth

definitions.meaning: the fleshy part of the face beside the mouth

explanation.surface: Insolent remarks muttered out of the corner of the mouth.
explanation.definitionFit: Cheek means sauciness, and it is also the fleshy wall of the face flanking the lips.

clue.text: The man, they say, for the' post

indicators.note: they say signals that the word is to be taken as it is spoken

parts.note: male describes a man

explanation.surface: Someone is described as the man for the postal job.
explanation.walkthrough: 'they say' marks a word heard rather than read: MALE sounds like the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Mail is letters and parcels sent through the postal service.

clue.text: Actors overshadowed by nameless girl as the queen

indicators.note: overshadowed by suggests the actors are covered over, enclosed by the girl's name
nameless means the letter N, an abbreviation for name, is removed

parts.note: Joan is a girl's name
a cast is the set of actors in a play

explanation.surface: A theatre company is upstaged by an unknown young woman playing a queen.
explanation.walkthrough: 'nameless' removes N, the usual abbreviation for name, leaving JOA; 'overshadowed by' then wraps it round the actors. Jocasta is a figure of Greek tragedy, Sophocles' Oedipus the King.
explanation.definitionFit: Jocasta is the queen of Thebes in Greek legend, mother and wife of Oedipus.

clue.text: Parties can become a slog

indicators.note: can become signals that the letters of parties are rearranged into something new

explanation.surface: Going to too many parties can turn into hard work.
explanation.walkthrough: 'can become' rearranges the letters of PARTIES.
explanation.definitionFit: A traipse is a long, wearisome walk, much like a trudge.

clue.text: Hand bringing the blood 'to Victoria's cheeks

definitions.meaning: a hand of cards; the best poker hand is ace to ten of one suit
a blush on the face of Queen Victoria would be a regal reddening

explanation.surface: Something that makes Queen Victoria blush.
explanation.walkthrough: The second reading is whimsical: a flush is a reddening of the face, and on Victoria's face it would be royal.
explanation.definitionFit: In poker the top-ranking hand is ace, king, queen, jack and ten of one suit; the second sense is a monarch's blush.

clue.text: The music for a reel

definitions.meaning: a style of popular music with a heavy beat
to reel is to sway or stagger

explanation.surface: Musical accompaniment for a Scottish dance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'reel' reads as a Scottish dance tune, but here it is the verb meaning to sway.
explanation.definitionFit: Rock is a genre of popular music, and to rock is to sway back and forth.

clue.text: US not following the rules

explanation.surface: America is accused of breaking the rules.
explanation.walkthrough: 'US' looks like America, but it is the abbreviation for unserviceable.
explanation.definitionFit: Broken equipment is labelled unserviceable, and improper behaviour is said to break the rules.

clue.text: Capital transport put out of order by bad weather

indicators.note: out of order signals the letters of put are jumbled

parts.note: rain is bad weather

explanation.surface: A city's trains are disrupted by a storm.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out of order' jumbles PUT into UPT. An up train is a British railway term for one travelling towards London, the capital.
explanation.definitionFit: British railways call a service heading towards London the up line, so its trains run toward the capital.

clue.text: Clings to a new order, while clinging to the old

indicators.note: a new order signals the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: People hold on to a new regime while others cling to the past.
explanation.walkthrough: 'new order' rearranges CLINGS TO A.
explanation.definitionFit: Nostalgic means wistfully longing for the past.

clue.text: Howl, a humdinger, around a note

indicators.note: around signals that the word for humdinger is turned to run backwards

parts.note: a lulu is an outstanding example, a humdinger
te is the seventh note of the sol-fa scale

explanation.surface: A tremendous howl circles one musical note.
explanation.walkthrough: 'around' turns the humdinger back to front, giving ULUL. 'humdinger' and 'lulu' are both informal words for something remarkable.
explanation.definitionFit: To ululate is to wail or cry out with a long trilling sound.

clue.text: Chinaman, for instance, always holds back

indicators.note: holds signals one piece is gripped inside another

parts.note: e'er is a poetic contraction of ever, meaning always
astern means towards the back of a ship

explanation.surface: A Chinese man, for example, always keeps something in reserve.
explanation.walkthrough: 'holds' wraps the poetic contraction for always round the nautical word for back. 'Chinaman' is an old, now offensive, term for a man from China.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone from China comes from the Orient, the eastern part of the world.

clue.text: Hero — he's got fat sitting around outside

indicators.note: outside tells us the reversed fat goes round the outside of he's
around signals the word for fat is turned to run backwards

parts.note: suet is hard animal fat used in cooking
taken as written, without the apostrophe

explanation.surface: A hero has gone to seed, lazing about outdoors and getting fat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'around' turns the fat backwards, giving TEUS, and 'outside' wraps it round he's; 'got' and 'sitting' are padding for the picture.
explanation.definitionFit: Theseus is the Greek legendary champion who slew the Minotaur.

clue.text: Wanting to copy' a bird, insect drops its tail

parts.note: the emu is a large flightless Australian bird

indicators.note: drops its tail means the last letter of the word for insect is removed

parts.note: a louse is a small parasitic insect

explanation.surface: Someone wants to imitate a bird, and an insect sheds its tail.
explanation.walkthrough: 'drops its tail' removes the final letter of the insect, leaving LOUS, after the bird.
explanation.definitionFit: Emulous means eager to rival or imitate someone.

clue.text: Outbreak of-fighting reduces the value of stocks, perhaps

indicators.note: the outbreak of something is its beginning, so the first letter of fighting

parts.note: to lower something is to reduce its value

explanation.surface: War breaking out sends the price of shares down.
explanation.walkthrough: 'stocks' suggests shares to fit the financial surface, but stocks are scented garden plants, so 'perhaps' marks them as one example.
explanation.definitionFit: Stocks are garden plants grown for their scented blooms, one example of blossoming plants.

clue.text: Down payment in his name to the auditors

indicators.note: auditors are listeners, so the word is taken as it sounds

parts.note: Ernest is a man's name

explanation.surface: A man's name is on the deposit, read out to the accountants.
explanation.walkthrough: 'auditors' suggests accountants, but here it means listeners.
explanation.definitionFit: An earnest is money paid in advance as a pledge of a bargain.

clue.text: Fruit that's sound, we hear

indicators.note: we hear signals the word is identified by how it is spoken

parts.note: to plumb is to sound or measure the depth of water

explanation.surface: Some fruit is described as being in good condition.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sound' looks like 'healthy', but it is the verb meaning to measure depth, PLUMB.
explanation.definitionFit: A plum is a stone fruit with smooth purple or yellow skin.

clue.text: It's all right in a' game

indicators.note: in signals one piece is placed inside another

parts.note: a, as in so much a head, means per
OK means all right

explanation.surface: Everything is fine within a game.
explanation.walkthrough: 'a' in the sense of 'ten pounds a head' is a classic crossword trick for per; 'It's' is only a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Poker is a card game of betting and bluffing.

clue.text: Part of a wall in the soup?

definitions.meaning: a waterproof layer laid in a brick wall to stop rising moisture
soup is a wet dish of a meal

explanation.surface: Asking whether some part of a wall is in trouble.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in the soup' reads as the idiom for being in trouble; split, the soup is a liquid serving of a meal.
explanation.definitionFit: A damp course is a moisture barrier near the foot of a wall, and soup is a wet stage of dinner.

clue.text: Tool has handle going to a point

parts.note: to paw is to handle roughly
N, north, is a point of the compass

explanation.surface: A tool whose handle tapers to a point.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tool' and 'handle' suggest an implement; a tool here is a person used by others.
explanation.definitionFit: A pawn is someone manipulated by others, a mere instrument.

clue.text: In speech, look for support

indicators.note: in speech signals the word is taken as it is spoken

parts.note: to peer is to look closely

explanation.surface: In a speech, someone looks for backing.
explanation.definitionFit: A pier is a pillar holding up a bridge or arch.

clue.text: Fly! There's a headless friar about, fly!

indicators.note: about signals the shortened word for friar is turned to run backwards
headless means the first letter of the word for friar is removed

parts.note: a monk is a member of a religious order, like a friar
to wing is to fly

explanation.surface: A frantic warning to flee from a ghostly friar without a head.
explanation.walkthrough: 'headless' cuts the friar to ONK and 'about' reverses that to KNO. 'Fly' as an adjective is slang for sharp or streetwise; the second 'fly' is the verb.
explanation.definitionFit: Fly is slang for shrewd and alert, meaning sharp and in the know.

clue.text: Duck winged? Duck cooked!

indicators.note: cooked signals the letters are mixed up, as food is changed by cooking

parts.note: a duck is a score of nothing in cricket, so the letter O

explanation.surface: A diner asks if the duck is a wing portion and is told it is cooked.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cooked' rearranges WINGED plus O, cricket's duck for zero.
explanation.definitionFit: The widgeon is a kind of dabbling wild duck.

clue.text: The others get stacked up, we hear, and bound

parts.note: the rest means the others

indicators.note: we hear signals the word is identified by how it is spoken

parts.note: ricked means stacked up, as hay is built into a rick

explanation.surface: Everyone else gets piled up and tied together.
explanation.walkthrough: A rick is a stack of hay, so ricked means stacked; said aloud it gives RICT.
explanation.definitionFit: To bound something is to set limits on it, to confine it.

clue.text: Boxer in depression?

definitions.meaning: one who packs things into crates
a hollow in the ground, as left by a meteor

explanation.surface: Is a fighter feeling low?
explanation.walkthrough: 'Boxer' suggests a fighter, but it is someone who puts goods into boxes.
explanation.definitionFit: A crater is a bowl-shaped hollow, and a crater is also whimsically one who crates goods.
